title: Escaped Nested Dictionary Paths
instructions:
Implement `parse_path` and `PathStore` in `paths.py`. Paths address dictionary keys only;
there is no list indexing. Values are JSON-like objects (dicts with string keys, lists,
strings, numbers, bool and None). A key may contain dots or backslashes.

`parse_path(path: str) -> list[str]` splits on unescaped dots. Backslash may escape only
`.` or `\`, producing that literal character in the key. Empty paths/segments, trailing
backslashes and any other escape raise `ValueError`. Whitespace is literal. For example
raw path `r'user.first\.name'` has keys `['user', 'first.name']`.

`PathStore(data: dict | None = None)` deep-copies data; None means an empty dict.
- `get(path: str, default=None)` returns a deep copy of the value, or a deep copy of default
  if any key is absent. Encountering a non-dict before the last key raises `TypeError`.
  A present None is a value, not a missing key.
- `set(path: str, value) -> None` creates missing intermediate dictionaries and deep-copies
  the value. Existing intermediate non-dicts raise `TypeError`. It may replace any final
  value, including a dictionary. Errors must leave the store unchanged.
- `delete(path: str) -> bool` deletes an existing final key, returning True. If any key is
  missing return False. Intermediate non-dicts raise `TypeError`. Do not prune empty parents.
- `snapshot() -> dict` returns a deep copy of the entire store.
All path operations use parse_path and reject invalid syntax before traversal or mutation.
Caller changes to constructor data, set values, or returned data must never affect the store.
